title: dual_track.py 2026-08-16: eight-gap overhaul, session mode, and first publication

concept.problem_being_solved: The generator's output on prior jobs exposed eight failure modes. The ERR-UI-004 document passed the old checks while containing self-congratulatory narration and a layman track that repeated the developer narrative in plainer words. The 2026-08-15 pfind session skipped rendering and validation entirely because `--validate` was opt-in. The tool also had no way to document work done in a directory — `code` mode reads current state, and work history lives in git and session notes, not in the source file.
concept.approach_taken: Close the gaps inside `dual_track.py` itself instead of relying on prompt discipline. Three structural additions (a `session` mode, `get_prior_doc_context()` injection, an idea-level separation check), one new ban list (`BANNED_SELF_CONGRAT`), one default flip (validation on unless `--no-validate`), and three prompt rewrites (`worst_case`, `known_alternatives`, `_CLAIM_SOURCING`). Then publish the folder as a git repository and run the tool on itself as its first end-to-end test.
concept.before_state: Before this session the script had two documentation modes (`code`, `release`), a marketing-only banned-phrase list, a syntax-only separation check, opt-in validation, and prompts that invited invented rationale and over-broad worst cases. The folder was not a git repository and existed only as one of three local copies.
concept.after_state: The script is 3283 lines with four modes (`code`, `session`, `release`, `precheck`) and validation on by default. The folder is a git repository with one commit (`b0b880d`) pushed to `github.com/gorillanobakaa-dot/dual-track-doc-generator`. The self-documentation in `docs-self/` is in a mixed state: the offline precheck ran (one P2 finding), the `code`-mode prep files exist, but their `.filled.json` files are thin stubs that no one rendered or validated. This session-mode run is the first fill that reaches the render-and-validate stage.
concept.known_alternatives: Not available in the source material. The commit message (`Add dual-track documentation generator source and self-docs`) records no rejected approaches, and the session notes name none.

decisions_made.decision: Enforce quality in code, not in prompts: ban lists, score checks, and schema enums live in `dual_track.py` where a model cannot talk its way around them.
decisions_made.reason: The README states the schema is 'the enforcement mechanism, not the prompt'.

decisions_made.decision: Flip validation from opt-in to opt-out on every render command.
decisions_made.reason: The 2026-08-15 session proved that even the tool's own `then_run` hint let users skip the gate.

decisions_made.decision: Rename `design_rationale` to `known_alternatives` and require 'Not available in the source material.' when rationale is undocumented.
decisions_made.reason: A model cannot recover design intent from an implementation, so the field invited invention.

decisions_made.decision: Publish the folder to GitHub as its own repository instead of leaving it as a local copy.
decisions_made.reason: The session notes record the publication but not the motive; a public home for the tool is the plausible reason.

decisions_made.decision: Leave the thin `code`-mode filled stubs in place instead of deleting them.
decisions_made.reason: The session notes cite the house rule that nothing is deleted; the stubs stay as evidence of the attempt.

tried_and_abandoned.why_abandoned: The fill was minimal — most reference arrays empty, one claim source each — and no one ran render or validation on it. The session notes judge that it would not pass the script's own gate. Abandoned instead of completed; the session-mode run supersedes it as the self-documentation path.

claimed_but_not_verified: The README states all three local copies (canonical, vault, Second Brain) are identical as of 2026-08-16. A `sha256sum` check during documentation DISPROVED this: the canonical and Second Brain copies match (3283 lines), but the vault copy is the 08:06 snapshot (3225 lines) and never received the final 08:57 version. The README's line-count header (3225) is also stale for the same reason.
The eight fixes are described in the README but have no end-to-end test evidence in the diff; this session-mode run is the first such test.
The `~/.local/bin/dual-track` symlink is stated to point at the canonical copy; the session records do not re-verify it.
